newsitem.title: UK: EASDAQ expects number of stocks to double by July.
newsitem.headline: EASDAQ expects number of stocks to double by July.

text.p: Pan-European new growth stock market EASDAQ said on Wednesday it expected the number of companies quoted on the exchange to double by the summer.
Speaking at a conference in London to promote the exchange, Erik Hallmann, head of admissions to EASDAQ, said he expected a further eight companies to be listed on EASDAQ by July.
The Brussels-based market opened in November last year with a view to attracting fast growing companies with international aspirations looking to raise capital.
But the fledgling European exchange is still tiny in terms of turnover and number of companies quoted when compared with its American role-model, NASDAQ, the New York-based stock exchange.
Eight companies are currently listed on EASDAQ with a combined market capitalisation of $1.29 billion. EASDAQ said a total of $356 million dollars had been raised by the flotations.
Anthony Preece, head of market operations, said the average daily turnover was between 150,000 and 200,000 shares representing $1 million to $1.5 million.
"The number of trades can vary enormously," said Preece. On one day there were 400 trades, but the exchange averages about 40 a day, he said.
Stocks on EASDAQ are traded over the telephone using a quote driven (market-maker) system designed to create maximum liquidity. It based its trading system on NASDAQ.
Hallmann said he was satisfied with liquidity for the stocks with a single listing on EASDAQ but liquidity was low for companies listed on both EASDAQ and NASDAQ.
EASDAQ said it aimed to provide a liquid, transparent and well regulated market for shares in growth companies with a high level of information disclosure.

The exchange said its criteria for the admission of companies to listing would not be compromised in an effort to gain more listings. It claimed thirty percent of applications for admission were rejected.
